title: TAPPaaS Site
description: The Site is the top-level umbrella for a TAPPaaS installation (ADR-007d). It holds site-wide identity, location, hardware (Proxmox nodes + their storage pools), backup target, update schedule, module catalog repositories, and references to the organization config files. Environments are NOT listed here — they are simply whatever is present under config/environments/*.json (enumerated from the directory, not from site.json). Domain, DNS, and identity are per-environment (NOT site-wide) and live in config/environments/*.json. site.json replaces configuration.json at cutover; during the phased migration both files may coexist. See ADR-007 P2.

name.description: Neutral site code (e.g. warmelo1 — place plus number). Aligned with the Proxmox cluster name at creation, informational afterwards (ADR-007d #426). Not used to name any environment, organization, or zone — those key on defaultEnvironment.

defaultEnvironment.description: Name of the default (tenant) environment — also its network zone and owner organization. Decoupled from the site code so site.name can be renamed with a single edit without touching any environment/org/zone (ADR-007d #426). Must be a valid zone/environment slug.

email.description: Installer/admin contact email (Let's Encrypt ACME account, people bootstrap). Carried over from configuration.json .tappaas.email during the S3b reader cutover.

location.description: Physical/legal location of the site, and the master data every module reads for time and locale (#408). The operator answers country/keyboard/timezone once, on the first Proxmox install; that node is the source these are derived from, not the mothership's own clock — a NixOS template, which is how a Danish site came to record NL/Europe/Amsterdam.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. DK). Derived from the timezone: the installer uses it but no Proxmox node stores it, so the timezone is what it is read back from.

timezone.description: IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/Copenhagen), as set on the first node.

locale.description: POSIX locale (e.g. en_US), as set on the first node.

keyboard.description: Console keyboard layout (e.g. dk), as set on the first node — its XKBLAYOUT. The PXE answer file and every OS family read it from here (#408); before this field the provisioner used a built-in default, which is why a node added later came up with 'us'.

city.description: City the Site is in — lets an off-site copy in the same country show it is elsewhere (#609, ADR-012 §1.5).

building.description: Building or data centre — for an off-site copy in the same city (#609).

latitude.description: Decimal degrees, north positive. Set by the operator — no node knows it. Read by locale-aware modules that need a position rather than a country (#348: Home Assistant's core config).

longitude.description: Decimal degrees, east positive. Set by the operator — no node knows it. Read by locale-aware modules that need a position rather than a country (#348: Home Assistant's core config).

network.description: Site WAN configuration. No rootDomain — domains are per-environment.

isp.description: ISP name, for operator reference only.

publicIp.description: Public IP address, or "auto" to discover at runtime.

hardware.description: Physical hardware: the Proxmox nodes that make up the cluster.

nodes.description: List of Proxmox nodes. nodeCount is computed from this array (no separate field).

storagePools.description: Storage pools available on this node (e.g. ["tanka1", "tankb1"]).

backup.description: Site-wide backup target. null when no backup is configured yet.

defaultRetention.description: Site-wide default backup retention period (e.g. 7y, 5y, 1y). The base of the Site -> Environment -> Module retention cascade (ADR-007 P9): environments and modules may override it.

offsiteResidency.description: Data residency of the offsite backup buddy (ADR-007 P9). Used by 'backup-manager validate' to reject backing an eu-only environment up to a non-EU offsite. eu-only by default; set global only when the offsite is outside the EU.

defaultSchedule.description: Site-wide default backup frequency and the base of the Site -> Environment -> Module schedule cascade (ADR-012 §3.2). One of 'daily' | 'weekly' | 'monthly', or a bare 'HH:MM' meaning daily at that time. Environments and modules may override it, but never with anything more frequent than once a day — that ceiling is the platform's, not a policy.

updateSchedule.description: Site-wide update schedule (ADR-017 D7). {frequency: none|daily|weekly|monthly, weekday: day name, hour: 0-23}. weekday is read only under weekly and monthly; hour defaults to 2. The legacy [period, day, hour] triple is still read, and migration 0003 rewrites it.

automaticReboot.description: Whether updates may reboot automatically. Site-wide until P3 (then moves to Environment).

snapshotRetention.description: Number of snapshots to retain. Site-wide until P3 (then moves to Environment).

repositories.description: Registry of checked-out repositories whose module catalogs back NAME-based module resolution (resolve-module.sh, ADR-004). This is NOT the only way a module is located and NOT required for a module to work: install-module.sh takes the current directory first, recording the module's source dir as .location in its deployed config, so a module installed from an unregistered path resolves through .location alone (issue #460).

branch.description: Branch tracked by the local checkout.

path.description: Absolute path of the local checkout. Load-bearing: resolve-module.sh skips any entry without it, so a repository lacking path contributes no modules to name-based resolution. Not in `required` only so site.json files written before it was declared still validate.

managed.description: full = the repository carries TAPPaaS modules and its catalog is validated on add; tracked = registered without catalog requirements.

catalog.description: Module catalog path, relative to the repository root. Written by `repository add` as the path it actually found (which may be the legacy src/modules.json) and read by resolve-module.sh. Absent means: try src/module-catalog.json, then legacy src/modules.json.
